name: Lukey
tagline: Not a leak. THE leaks. Plural. He's a franchise. And you're trespassing.
notes: Stats run 0-20 (clamped). Ending thresholds: stay = romance >= 16 && friction < 8; let him go (loved) = romance >= 16; friends = friendship >= 14 && friction < 8; he uses your real name in Act 4 if romance >= 12 going in; otherwise 'That's your call' gives the friends ending if friction < 8, or the grumpy ending if friction >= 8. Week 1 never mentions the other guys; from week 2 each act has at most two housemate references. Optional jealousy choices read malcolm/tyler/wyatt.romance (>= 5 in Act 2, >= 7 in Act 3). The dehumidifier is just an appliance (no name). Inspector Dan never visits during the weekly acts (he only comes on day 30, in inspection.json). Sets flag.lukey_both (v1), flag.lukey_realfix (v3), flag.lukey_blackout (v3, Wyatt's blackout) and flag.lukey_human (v4_reveal).

romance_success.title: Head Over Heels Over Pipes
romance_success.text: Lukey stayed. He's dry, he's solid, his curls are ENORMOUS and he is absolutely gone on you. He still fills your coffee pot from across the room every morning. Out of love. He also moved the dehumidifier to the garage. Out of spite.

romance_failure.title: Love You to the Last Drop
romance_failure.text: He loved you enough to go. All that's left is a heart-shaped drop on the kitchen floor that never quite dries. You'd never mop it anyway. You keep the dehumidifier on the other side of the room, just in case.

friend_success.title: Pipe Dreams Come True
friend_success.text: Lukey finally got his date (a 'frate,' technically), finished his business and passed on in a puff of warm steam that smelled faintly of copper. He left the kitchen spotless. Brenda would be proud. Probably.

friend_failure.title: Fixed It Myself (Mostly)
friend_failure.text: Lukey passed on a little grumpy, a lot proud and fully convinced he did all the work. ('You held the flashlight.') The house is dry. The windows are dry. Everyone's dry. Nobody's thrilled.

lines: *{sfx:WaterSplash} A gush of water bursts from under the sink, and a big, broad man slides out on the wave. Wet copper curls. A short auburn beard. A soaked white tank top with a red valve wheel where his heart should be. His arms and legs are copper pipe, green at the joints, patched here and there with silver duct tape. He looks you up and down with deep disappointment.*
Oh, great. Another one.
Let me guess. Flipper. Gray paint, 'open plan,' a little wooden sign that says LIVE LAUGH LOVE. You're going to gut my house and sell it to a couple called Jasper and Pip.
Last flipper wanted everything white. White walls, white floors, white EVERYTHING. Lasted one day.
Name's Lukey. I'm the leaks around here. Not A leak. THE leaks. Plural. I'm a [franchise]. And you're trespassing.

choices.text: It's my house now. I bought it.
Wow. You're very rude for a water stain. Cute, though.
I'm not gutting anything. I'm fixing what's broken.

lines: Kitchen sink? Headquarters. Bathroom ceiling? Penthouse. Great acoustics. East wall? Summer home. Hall radiator? Vacation home. I share it with a dead moth called [Gerald]. He's very quiet. Better company than you.
And you're about to evict every single one of us. For PROFIT.

choices.text: It's my house now. I bought it.
Rude AND a property mogul. Cute, though.
I'm not evicting anyone. I'm fixing what's broken.

lines: You: Is Gerald... okay?
He's a MOTH, landlady. He's been dead since the first Bush administration. He's thriving.
Bought it. With MONEY. Like that means anything. I've lived here thirty-nine years, Barbie. What've you got? A drill and a business card?
*{sfx:TapDrip} He drips, very pointedly, onto your business card.*
*{sfx:TapDrip} Drip-drip-drip-drip.*
Don't. Don't do that. Don't make it weird. I am being HOSTILE.
...Your hair's nice. Get out of my house.
'Fixing what's broken.' That's what they all say. Then it's gray paint and a feature wall.
I've seen your type, landlady. You don't love houses. You love the RECEIPT.
Go on, then. How much are you flipping it for? What's my home worth to you?

choices.text: Honestly? Enough to cover my mortgage and then some. That's the job.
Everything I've got. My savings are in this place.
Are you always this grumpy, or is it the damp?

lines: *{sfx:WaterSplash} Every tap in the kitchen turns on at once.*
'And then some.' Great. Super. Thirty-nine years of my life, and I'm a line item.
Well, here's a line item for you, landlady. Every leak you fix is a piece of ME gone. You're not just flipping a house. You're flipping ME.
*The dripping hesitates.*
...All of it? That's stupid. That's a really stupid thing to do with savings.
Still doesn't make it yours. And here's the catch, landlady: every leak you fix is a piece of ME gone.
I'm not grumpy. I'm DAMP. And yes, it's the damp. It's always the damp.
Also, every leak you fix is a piece of me gone. So forgive me if I'm not throwing you a housewarming.
So here's how this goes. You fix something, I break something. You patch a wall, I flood your shoes. It's called a working relationship.

choices.text: Fine. Game on, leak.
Or we could find something that works for both of us.
You know I can just call a plumber, right?

lines: Game on. Ooh. Okay. I love a little competition. Fair warning: I'm extremely petty and I have NOTHING else to do.
*Lukey will remember that.*
Both of us? Ha. Adorable. That's what they all say, landlady. Right before they paint the whole house a color called 'Swiss Coffee.'
...It's WHITE, landlady. They named a white after COFFEE.
*But the drip slows down. Just a little.*
*Lukey will remember that.*
A PLUMBER? You'd bring a PLUMBER into this house?
*{sfx:WaterSplash} A jet of water hits you square in the face.*
That's for even saying it.
And what's the RUSH? You've been banging around since dawn like the place is on fire. It's not on fire. I'd know. I'd put it out.
You: The city inspects this house on day thirty. If it doesn't pass, they bulldoze it.
*The dripping stops dead.*
...Bulldoze. As in BULLDOZER. As in my headquarters, my penthouse, my summer home and my vacation home in one big wet pile.
Thirty days? Nobody fixes this place in thirty days. I've been leaking for thirty-nine YEARS.

choices.text: Watch me.
Then help me. If the house passes, you get to keep it.
Relax. Thirty days is plenty. I'm good with my hands.

lines: Ooh. 'Watch me.' Okay, landlady. I'll watch. From INSIDE THE WALLS.
*Drip. Drip. Dripdripdripdrip.*
...That came out creepier than I meant. I meant it supportively. No I didn't. I don't know what I meant.
Help you. Help you DELETE me, one leak at a time. Great deal. Love it.
*{sfx:PipeClank} Somewhere in the walls, something gurgles nervously.*
...I don't love bulldozers either, though. I'll think about it. Thinking's free. I've got nothing BUT time.
'Good with my hands.' Oh, EVERYBODY says that in this kitchen, landlady. Right before something goes horribly—
*He stops. He frowns at the pipe under the sink like it owes him money. Then he shrugs it off.*
Anyway. You'll fail. Bulldozer. Big wet pile. I'll be in it.
*He glares at the box you've just unpacked: a brand-new dehumidifier. You plug it in. {sfx:Hum} It hums. A little green light comes on.*
What. Is. THAT.

choices.text: A dehumidifier. It's going to dry out your walls.
Relax. It's just here to help with the damp.
Jealous? It's very quiet. Very low maintenance. Unlike some people.

lines: Dry out the— those are MY WALLS. That's my SUMMER HOME. You've bought an assassin. A little white plastic assassin with a carry handle.
*The bucket gurgles. Lukey shudders.*
It's drinking me. I can FEEL it drinking me.
'Help with the damp.' I AM the damp! That's like bringing a Shop-Vac to a dust bunny's birthday party!
Low MAINTENANCE? It's got a WATER TANK, landlady. It's high maintenance with a carry handle.
*He glares at the little green light like it said something. It didn't. It's a dehumidifier.*

*He turns to slide back under the sink and leaves a big puddle on the tiles. You reach past him to shut off the tap, step right in it, and your foot goes out from under you. {sfx:Squelch} He lunges to catch you. For one second there's a cold, wet arm around your waist. Then it's just water, and you sit down hard in the puddle. {sfx:WaterSplash}*
Ha. Can't even catch you. Can't even touch me. Good. Keep it that way. Nobody touches the leaks.
*He stares at his own copper arm like it did something without asking.*
...You okay? Not that I care. That's MY puddle. You dented it.
...You've got a little drywall in your hair. Not that I'm looking. Get out of my kitchen.
You said 'both of us.' Last week. I thought about it.
It's still stupid. ...I thought about it a LOT. Moving on.
Oh. It's you. Barbie. I flooded your shoes twice this week. You're welcome.
...Fine. Truce. For today. Only because that dehumidifier hums all night and I need someone to complain to.
*There's a new damp patch on the kitchen wall. It looks suspiciously like a heart. When you walk in, it gets bigger. When you look at it, it gets smaller, fast.*
You patched the bathroom. I can't feel my left side. Thanks for that, boss.
*He meant 'boss' to sound sarcastic. It didn't quite.*
I had a VIEW up there. Best seat in the house. Now it's just ceiling. Dry, boring, beige ceiling.
Also, your dehumidifier drank half my summer home. You empty a bucket of me into the yard every MORNING, boss. I'm in the HYDRANGEAS now. I'm MULCH.
And those podcast ladies think I'm a [catfish].

choices.text: Is that damp patch... a heart?
For the record, you're the least fish-like thing I've ever met.
The dehumidifier is doing a great job, actually.

lines: You: Bev seems really committed to the catfish thing.
I'm not a catfish. ...Am I a catfish?
I'm not wet in a fish way. I'm wet in a SEXY way.
What heart? That's a STAIN. A very romantic stain. Walls do that. Shut up.
*It throbs. Slightly.*
THANK you. No scales. I've got ABS. I think. Hard to tell, I'm mostly drip.
*{sfx:Hum} The dehumidifier hums. Lukey glares at it like it hummed at him personally.*
It's a BUCKET that drinks ME, boss. One day it'll be just you, a dehumidifier and an empty bucket, and you'll miss me.
Anyway. East wall's next, isn't it? My SUMMER HOME. I object. I'd put it in writing, but you keep wiping the windows.
...But if you're going in, you need me. I know every drip in that wall. Been there since 1986. Er— since forever. Since INSTALLATION.
*He's humming 'Livin' on a Prayer' while he says it.*

choices.text: Lukey, how does a leak know Bon Jovi?
Since 1986? That's weirdly specific.
Show me where. I'll take the help.

lines: Everyone knows Bon Jovi. It's in the water. Literally. I'm the water.
*He does a small, completely unconscious Running Man.*
Is it? Big year for leaks. Excellent vintage. Shoulder pads were huge. For pipes. Pipe shoulder pads. Drop it.
Oh, NOW she wants my help. When it's my summer home on the line.
...Second stud from the left. Watch the wire. And the wasp nest. That's Kevin. Kevin's harmless.

*You open up the east wall together. He talks you through every drip with a wet finger, very close to your ear, being extremely bossy about it. Every time your wrench gets near the wiring he yells 'WYATT'S! DON'T!' like a lifeguard.*
*It is the most romantic plumbing you have ever done. Neither of you says so.*
*When it's done, the summer home is dry, and Lukey looks more THERE. Less drizzle, more man.*
Huh. Fewer leaks, less of me spread around. I'm... concentrated. Like an orange juice.

choices.text: You look good concentrated.
Does it hurt? Losing a leak?
Great. Two down, two to go.

lines: *He checks his reflection in the toaster. He likes what he sees.*
I DO look good. Has this jawline been here the whole time?
Nah. It tickles. Like losing a sock. Except the sock is your summer home.
...Thanks for asking, though. Nobody ever asks the leaks how they're doing.
Counting down. Like New Year's Eve. Except at midnight I'm gone and you get drywall.
*A slow, sarcastic drip.*
*Afterward you sit on the kitchen floor together. You're covered in drywall dust. On him it's turned to paste, and his curls are full of it.*
*{sfx:TapDrip} Across the room, the coffee pot fills itself. One cup. Not a drop spilled. The mug slides along the counter on a little wave and stops right by your hand.*
Don't read into it. You looked thirsty. Leaks are very hospitable.
So. Boss. When this place is done, then what? Where does a flipper go when she runs out of house?

choices.text: Lukey. Is this a coffee date?
Somewhere with a kitchen I don't have to fix.
Honestly? Onto the next one. That's the job.
You're not the only guy in this house who's been sweet to me, you know.

lines: A DATE? Please. It's coffee. In my day we called this 'grabbing a milkshake.'
*He freezes.*
In my day? What day? Leaks don't have days. Forget I said that.
Ha! Good luck. Every kitchen needs fixing, boss. That's the beauty of kitchens.
...This one, for example. Very fixable. Great light. Original sink. Not an offer. It's a sales pitch. I'm being a realtor.
*The coffee goes cold. Instantly. He did that.*
The next one. Sure. Must be nice, having a next one.
Sweet to— boss. I live IN the walls. I hear EVERYTHING.
It's fine. It's a free market. We're rival franchises.
...But I've been here longest, I've got the most locations, and I'm the only one who can fill your coffee pot from across the room. Just saying.
*Your phone rings. Your realtor. You step into the hall, but the pipes run through every wall in this house.*
You: East wall's done. Kitchen's last. Then we rip the whole thing out. Open plan, white cabinets, gray floors. Nobody wants a 1987 kitchen.
You: List it the day it passes, sell to whoever pays most, and I'm onto the next one. That's the job.
*{sfx:WaterSplash} When you come back, every tap in the house is running. Lukey is standing in the middle of the kitchen, very solid and very still.*
Rip it out. Gray floors. Whoever pays most.
WHITE CABINETS? Why don't you paint the whole place Swiss Coffee while you're at it!
This is a HOME, boss. People laughed in this kitchen. People had dates in this kitchen. Something happened in this kitchen. I don't know what. But it MATTERED.
And you want to turn it into a showroom for Jasper and Pip.

choices.text: It's not personal. Everything I own is riding on this flip. If it fails, I lose it all.
Houses are investments, Lukey. That's how the world works.
...You're right. I've been treating your home like a spreadsheet.

lines: Everything? So it's your home on the line, or mine. Awesome. Great. Love that for us.
*The taps shut off, one by one.*
I get it. I do. Doesn't mean I have to like you right now.
An INVESTMENT.
*The heart-shaped patch on the wall shrinks to nothing.*
Thirty-nine years, and I'm an investment. Get out of my kitchen, landlady.
*He blinks. He was ready for a fight. He was not ready for that.*
...Don't do that. Don't be reasonable when I'm angry. It's very confusing.
I still need a few days to be a sulky leak about it.

*He sinks into the walls. For the next few days the house is silent. No drips. No puns. The dehumidifier's bucket stays bone dry. It's the quietest this house has been in thirty-nine years, and you hate it.*

*{sfx:PowerDown} The power's out. Just this house; the rest of Heartbreak Lane is lit up like Christmas. From the fuse box in the living room comes a muffled, very apologetic voice: 'That wasn't me!' It was him.*
*You light candles in the kitchen. The house has been silent for three days, and you fixed the hall radiator alone.*
*{sfx:TapDrip} Then, very quietly, the tap drips once.*
Hi. Boss. Hi. I wasn't sulking, by the way. I was RESTING. In the walls. For three days. Leaks rest.
...You did my vacation home without me. [Gerald]'s gone. I'm down to one sink. Just me and the P-trap.
It's no fun dripping when nobody's around to be annoyed by it. I dripped on the dehumidifier. It didn't even notice. It's a DEHUMIDIFIER.
Anyway. I've been thinking. A leak's got a lot of time to think. Turns out you're not wrong. Houses cost money. Somebody has to fix them, and you're good at it. Annoyingly good.
But a house isn't just walls and grout, boss. It's whoever's in it. Right now that's me, a wasp called Kevin and, unfortunately, you.

choices.text: Then let's fix it properly. Not cheap. Whoever buys it gets a real home.
I missed you. The house was too quiet.
I still have to sell it, Lukey.

lines: You: I'm sorry about Gerald.
Thanks. He's in a better place. The trash can. He'd want me to move on.
*A small, brave drip.*
Properly. No gray floors?
You: No promises on the floors.
*He laughs, a real one, and the heart-shaped patch on the wall comes back bigger than ever.*
...Okay. Deal. Sweetheart. Whatever. I'm calling you sweetheart now. It's happening.
*The drip stops. Then it goes drip-drip-drip-drip-drip.*
You missed ME? The leak? The one who flooded your shoes?
...I missed you too. Don't make it a thing. Sweetheart.
Yeah. I know.
*He's quiet for a moment.*
Then sell it to someone who'll love it. Not Jasper and Pip. Promise me that, and we're square, sweetheart.
*Candles. A box of pasta. He 'cooks' by filling the pot from across the room with surgical precision and giving you terrible advice about salt.*
This isn't a date, by the way. Two adults. Candles. Spaghetti. Purely coincidental.
I did the water glasses. Filled them to the exact same line. Took me an hour. I don't know why a leak cares about [table settings|glasses].
Did you hear the podcast? Mrs. Pruitt next door says someone's been singing [Bon Jovi|bonjovi] in the walls. Ridiculous. I don't sing. I RESONATE.

choices.text: It's definitely a date. Sing for me.
Do you ever wonder why you know all this 80s stuff?
You definitely sing. You're terrible.
You know I'm seeing other people in this house too, right?

lines: You: Since when does a leak care about table settings?
Since always? Since... some dinner I never got to?
*He frowns. Something almost comes back to him. Then he shakes his head, and his wet curls spray the tablecloth.*
Nope. Weird thought. Gone. Eat your pasta.
Sweetheart. I know. The walls are VERY thin and I am IN them.
*He refills your glass from across the room without spilling a drop. He's stalling.*
And it's fine. Really. I'm a grown man. Probably. Nobody in this house is exclusive. It's a free market.
...But I'm your favorite. Don't answer that. The patch on the wall already knows.
*He hums the first line of 'Livin' on a Prayer.' Then the second. Then he's doing the guitar solo with a ladle.*
Okay. I resonate a LOT.
*He sings 'Livin' on a Prayer' into a wooden spoon. He hits none of the notes. He commits completely.*
*When he gets to 'take my hand,' he holds his out.*
Wonder? Leaks absorb culture. Through the walls. Like a sponge. A very cultured sponge.
*He goes quiet for a second.*
...Sometimes I dream about leg warmers. Is that normal for plumbing?
TERRIBLE? I'm a SOPRANO, sweetheart. You just can't hear it over the dripping.
*He sings one very high note. A wine glass cracks. He looks delighted.*
*He's reaching for you across the counter. There's only one leak left in the house, so there's finally enough of him in one place.*
*His hand doesn't pass through yours. It's cool and a little damp, the brass rivets on his fingers are cold, and it is very definitely a hand.*
...Oh. Hello.

choices.text: Hold on to it.
Lukey! You're solid!
Your hand is clammy.

lines: *He does. Neither of you says anything for a while. The candles flicker. The last leak drips, very slowly, very happily.*
First thing I've held in years that wasn't a P-trap. Kind of an upgrade, sweetheart.
Mostly solid! Like Jell-O! Handsome Jell-O!
*He squeezes your hand, then pokes his own face to check.*
I'm a LEAK. What did you expect, a hand lotion commercial?
*But he doesn't let go.*
*{sfx:PowerUp} The lights stutter back on. {sfx:RadioStatic} The radio crackles to life: 'BIG STORM SATURDAY. Heavy rain and flooding expected.'*
*Every candle flame in the room shivers. So does Lukey.*
Flooding. I don't like flooding. For leak reasons. Very normal leak reasons.

choices.text: Whatever happens, we'll handle it together.
A leak that's scared of floods? That's like a fish scared of the sea.
It's just rain. Pull yourself together.

lines: Together. Yeah. Leak and Flipper. Season finale. Big storm episode.
*He squeezes your hand. He's still holding it. He forgot to let go. He's not going to.*
Don't bring fish into this. Bev's already got me down as a catfish.
...But yeah. Weird, right? Something about it makes my curls go flat. My curls NEVER go flat.
I AM together. I'm the most together I've been in years. Literally. I'm down to one sink.
*Drip. Sulky drip.*
*Steam from the pasta pot fogs up the kitchen window. Letters start to appear in it, one at a time: 'L +'*
*They stop. Then someone rubs them out, very fast.*
That wasn't me. That was condensation. Condensation does that. It's science.

choices.text: Finish what you were writing.
Lukey, stop writing on my windows.
Please don't draw on the glass. I'm staging this place.

lines: It's not writing, it's COMMUNICATION. The window's basically my phone.
*The window fogs up again: 'sorry x'*
*{sfx:Hum} The dehumidifier kicks on and the glass clears. Lukey glares at it across the room.*
*The window fogs up again. In very neat letters: 'L + THE KITCHEN SINK.' Then, smaller, underneath: '+ U (MAYBE)'*
*He stares at the pasta like it's the most interesting pasta in the world.*
Don't look at it. I'm drying it. Look at the spaghetti, sweetheart. Look at the spaghetti.
*The window fogs up with a single, devastated word: 'WOW.'*
*A drip runs down the glass like a tear. It's a little much. It's working, though.*
*Late. The candles are stubs. He's sitting on the counter, swinging his copper-pipe legs, his work boots thumping the cabinet door.*
Sweetheart... I don't really know what I am. A leak. A bunch of leaks. One leak now. Whatever.
But I like who I am when you're here.
*A beat.*
That's the only sappy thing I'm saying this month. Goodnight. And unplug that dehumidifier. It drinks me in my sleep.
*Saturday morning. Storm clouds over Heartbreak Lane. Lukey is sitting on the kitchen floor, very still and very solid. For once, he isn't grinning.*
{player}.
*It's the first time he's ever used your real name. It sounds good in his mouth. He looks like he's been practicing.*
{player}, did you listen to the podcast?
*Saturday morning. Storm clouds over Heartbreak Lane. Lukey is sitting on the kitchen floor, very still and very solid. For once, he isn't grinning.*
Sweetheart. Did you listen to the podcast?
'Local aerobics instructor Luke Moretti, 34, died in 1987 when a cast-iron pipe fell on his head as he attempted to repair a woman's sink before their first date.'
That's me. I'm not a leak. I'm a GUY. I'm a guy who died SHOWING OFF.
Her name was Brenda. This was HER house. Not mine. I showed up early with a mixtape, her sink was dripping, and I said, 'Relax, babe. I'm great with my hands.'
She went upstairs to finish her hair. I dove under the sink, gave the pipe one big, manly lefty-loosey, and about ninety pounds of cast iron came down on my head. {sfx:Bonk} Bonk.
*He puts his face in his hands. They're very solid hands now.*
I died in LYCRA, sweetheart. Under BRENDA'S SINK. I told you I'd lived here thirty-nine years. I was here for TWENTY MINUTES.

*He looks down at himself: the soaked tank top, the denim cut-offs, copper pipe where his arms and legs used to be. Not a scrap of Lycra. Somewhere along the way, the house rebuilt him out of plumbing.*
Thirty-nine years dressed as a SINK. And somehow that's the LESS embarrassing outfit.

choices.text: For what it's worth, I bet you looked great in Lycra.
Lukey. You're a PERSON. That's huge.
Laugh. You can't help it.

lines: *He peeks through his fingers.*
...I did look great. Legs like a racehorse. Shiny. Teal.
I know. I KNOW. I have a birthday! I have a star sign! I'm probably a Leo. I'm DEFINITELY a Leo.
Oh, laugh it up. It IS hilarious. 'Man dies trying to impress woman with plumbing.' It's a Darwin Award with great hair.
*He's laughing too. A little. Despite himself.*
And the worst part? I never got the date. Brenda came downstairs with her hair done, and I was... busy. Being dead.
No wonder I hated you on sight. You were going to rip out this kitchen. The one place I nearly had a date.
And [Malcolm|malcolm] KNEW. He's been telling me for YEARS. I thought it was a mold thing.
Thirty-nine years of dripping, and I think that's it. That's why I'm still here. I never got my date.

choices.text: Then let's fix this sink, and I'll take you on that date.
We'll get you your date. Even if it's just as friends.
Can we focus on the sink? The storm's here.

lines: You: To be fair, he did keep saying it.
'Thou art a dead man's tears.' I thought he was just being GOTH about it!
...Wait. If I'm a guy, then is Malcolm a— is everybody in this house a— nope. No. One existential crisis per storm.
*The last leak goes drip-drip-drip-drip so fast it's basically a tap.*
A date. With you. Okay. YES. Brenda who? I mean— God bless Brenda. Great gal. Anyway. YES.
A friend date. A FRATE. Yeah. I'd like that. No pressure. Some pressure. I'm water, everything's pressure.
Right. Sink. Storm. The exact sink that killed me. No pressure.

*{sfx:Thunder} The storm hits. {sfx:Rain} Rain hammers the windows. All over the house, things creak, crack, flicker and drip at once. {sfx:PipeClank} The kitchen sink, the last leak, the one that started it all, groans, shudders and sprays.*
*The dehumidifier's bucket fills in seconds, and its little light goes red: FULL. For the first time, Lukey looks at the thing with something like respect.*
WYATT! If you're anywhere near here, STAY OUT OF THE KITCHEN! Water! Electricity! We've TALKED about this! Love you, buddy!
Okay! This is it! Righty-tighty! Lefty-loosey is how I DIED! And watch the [cast iron|pipe] over your head!
*You get under the sink together. He can't hold the wrench, but he knows every inch of that pipe. You're his hands. He's your eyes. Nobody is getting bonked today.*

choices.text: Talk me through it, instructor.
I trust you. Show me.
Step back. I've got this.

lines: You: Wait. Is that... THE pipe?
Same pipe. Thirty-nine years. We've been roommates this whole time.
I want to forgive it. I'm not there yet.
INSTRUCTOR. Okay! Quarter turn! And REACH! And TWIST! Feel the burn! Engage your core!
That last bit's aerobics. Ignore it. Actually don't, your core looks great.
*He puts his hands over yours on the wrench. Bolt by bolt. His voice is steady and soft the whole time.*
There. Feel that? That's the last one. You did it, sweetheart.
*You do it yourself. It takes three tries and a lot of swearing. He hovers, hands half-raised, not quite helping.*
...You held the wrench right. I'll give you that.
*{sfx:PipeClank} Thunk. Squeak. Silence.*
*Outside, the storm rages. Inside, for the first time in thirty-nine years, there isn't a single leak in the house. {sfx:SwitchOff} The dehumidifier clicks off. Nothing left to drink.*
*Lukey looks down at himself. Not one drop. His tank top is dry. His beard is dry. And his curls, for the first time since 1987, are DRY. They are ENORMOUS.*
...Oh my god. The VOLUME. Sweetheart, look at the volume.
*By nightfall the storm has blown itself out. The house is quiet and dry, and every tap in it is minding its own business.*

*You set the table. Candles. Wine. Bon Jovi on the stereo. Lukey has made an effort: fresh duct tape, brass couplings polished to a shine, boots double-knotted, and his see-through tank top has been [ironed|blazer].*
*He's even made a mixtape. Nobody knows how. The label says FOR BRENDA, with BRENDA crossed out and your name written over it in big loopy letters.*
So. This is it. The date. Thirty-nine years in the making.
